title: Radio to the IWRL6432BOOST radar by eight wires, page 1 of 2: the radio's end
warning: Unplug the radar's USB first. Each tag says where that wire's other end goes (page 2). Same colour both ends.
credit: Board drawing: TI SWRU633 Figure 2-1, leader lines removed

label: Red: pin 1 (3V3) to the radar's J2 pin 1
Black: pin 20 (GND) to the radar's J2 pin 7
Power first. Pin 1 is the top of the left outer
row; pin 20 is the top of the right outer row.
Yellow: pin 7 (SCLK) to J2 pin 5
Green: pin 15 (PICO) to J2 pin 2
Blue: pin 14 (POCI) to J2 pin 3
White: pin 18 (CS_N) to J2 pin 4
Pin 7: 7th socket down the left outer row.
14, 15, 18: count up the right outer row
from pin 11 at the bottom (20 is the top).
Orange: pin 36 (RESET_N) to J9 pin 1
Purple: pin 23 (SPI_INT) to J2 pin 6
Pin 23 is the 3rd socket down the left inner row.
Pin 36 is the 5th down the right inner row.
Leave the two P2 shunts (LED links) as shipped.

task_facts.head: For this step
items: Makes the radar chip's Cortex-M4F the radio's host over its own SPI A port, with the radar left alone
The radar's BoosterPack sockets (J8 and J9) sit on the back and carry no 3.3 V out, so the power and five of the signals come from the SPI header J2 on the top edge
A radio version line on the radar's USB serial port ending in 1, then one packet a second reaching the CC1354P10
